audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph Transjordanian tribal genealogies, wars, plunder, and Assyrian deportation, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Reuben and birthright, sexual transgression and descendant stigma, Joseph/Judah roles, Hagarite war, captive and livestock plunder, war-of-Divine claim, gendered infidelity metaphor, and Assyrian deportation.

verses.restored: Sons of Reuben firstborn of Israel—for he was firstborn, but because he profaned his father's bed, his birthright was given to sons of Joseph son of Israel, though genealogy was not reckoned according to birthright;
for Judah became strong among his brothers, and from him came a ruler, but birthright belonged to Joseph—
sons of Reuben firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
Descendants of Joel: Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, Shimei his son,
Micah his son, Reaiah his son, Baal his son,
Beerah his son, whom Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria carried into exile; he was leader of Reubenites.
His brothers by families, when genealogies of generations were enrolled: Jeiel the chief and Zechariah,
and Bela son of Azaz son of Shema son of Joel, who lived in Aroer as far as Nebo and Baal-meon.
Eastward he lived as far as entrance of wilderness from Euphrates River, because their livestock multiplied in land of Gilead.
In days of Saul they made war with Hagarites, who fell by their hand, and they lived in their tents throughout east of Gilead.
Children of Gad lived opposite them in land of Bashan as far as Salecah:
Joel the chief, Shapham second, Jaanai, and Shaphat in Bashan.
Their brothers by ancestral house: Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber—seven.
These were sons of Abihail son of Huri son of Jaroah son of Gilead son of Michael son of Jeshishai son of Jahdo son of Buz.
Ahi son of Abdiel son of Guni was head of their ancestral house.
They lived in Gilead, Bashan and its towns, and all pasturelands of Sharon to their limits.
All were enrolled in days of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel.
Sons of Reuben, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh—warriors bearing shield and sword, drawing bow, and trained for war—numbered forty-four thousand seven hundred sixty going out to battle.
They made war against Hagarites, Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.
They were helped against them, and Hagarites and all with them were given into their hand, because they cried to Divine in battle and Divine was entreated by them, because they trusted.
They captured their livestock: fifty thousand camels, two hundred fifty thousand sheep, two thousand donkeys, and one hundred thousand human beings.
Many fell slain, because narrator calls war from Divine; they lived in their place until exile.
Children of half-tribe of Manasseh lived in land and multiplied from Bashan to Baal-hermon, Senir, and mount Hermon.
Heads of their ancestral houses: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel—mighty warriors, renowned men, heads of ancestral houses.
They acted unfaithfully toward Divine of their ancestors and went after gods of peoples of land, whom Divine/narrator says were destroyed before them.

Divine of Israel stirred spirit of Pul king of Assyria, that is Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, and he carried Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh into exile, bringing them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and river Gozan, to this day.

translation_notes: Reuben's act concerns his own responsibility; descendants must not inherit sexual shame or reduced human worth.
Birthright, rulership, and genealogy are distinct social claims, not biological rankings.
Hagarites, Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab are human communities, not timeless enemies or modern ethnic categories.
Verse 21 counts one hundred thousand human captives alongside animals. People are not plunder, inventory, or evidence of blessing.
The claim that the war was from Divine reflects the Chronicler's theology and must be morally audited rather than used to sanctify conquest.
Military skill and large troop numbers are recorded, not endorsed as the highest form of communal value.
Sexualized language for religious unfaithfulness can reinforce misogyny and stigma toward sex workers; it should be translated and taught carefully.
Assyrian deportation is imperial forced displacement, not merely an abstract spiritual consequence.
Pul/Tiglath-pileser identification, numbers, place names, and genealogies require historical and textual audit.
safety_note: Do not use this chapter to justify inherited shame, anti-Arab or anti-Hagarite hatred, holy war, enslavement, human trafficking, seizure of civilian property, or victim-blaming of deported peoples. People counted among spoil remain people.
